verdict.rationale: Sentry documents rule-based alerts that fire when issues (from projects or Monitors) match pre-defined rules. Those alerts can route notifications to destinations such as a team's Slack channel, PagerDuty, tickets, or webhooks. The evidence covers only issue- and Monitor-based alerting, not alerting on any telemetry signal such as arbitrary traces, logs, or metrics, and it does not document grouping or silencing of notifications. Missing for 10: alerting on arbitrary telemetry signals (traces/logs/metrics), notification grouping/deduplication controls, silencing/muting/snooze of alerts, richer routing-rule documentation, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an SRE, I can alert on any telemetry signal with routing, grouping, and silencing of notifications

citations.quote: Sentry's **Alerts** take action when issues in your organization match pre-defined rules.
An alert can send notifications, create tickets, call webhooks, or use other integrations for issues coming from projects or Monitors.
Send a notification to your team's Slack channel when a new issue is created.
Get paged by important issues with PagerDuty.
